profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record identifies a commercial building at 5635 South Avenue in Boardman, a township adjoining Youngstown in Ohio's Mahoning Valley, tagged as a data center under the name Carrier Services Group. The name points toward telecommunications carrier support work, such as interconnection, switching, or managed network services for other telecom providers, which would be a genuine, if specialized and small scale, category of telecom infrastructure rather than an unrelated business. The Mahoning Valley carries a mix of legacy industrial and telecommunications infrastructure from its manufacturing history, so a facility supporting regional carrier operations in Boardman is plausible on its face. The matching carrierservicesgroup dot com domain does resolve, but it redirects to a bare parking page rather than an active company site describing services, location, or clients, so it could not be used to confirm what actually operates at this address. No independent business registration, press coverage, or alternate operator website could be matched to the name or address. This entry is published as an honest account of what could and could not be confirmed, rather than a guess in either direction, and will be updated if a verifiable operator or business description becomes available.

No other operator lead could be reached (search engines and archive.org blocked by egress policy). Cannot confirm operator.

reading.body:
Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities but published power specifications for only 8 of them, totaling 60.4 MW. The state's disclosed capacity is concentrated in a small number of sites, and the rest, including this one, cannot be ranked or compared.

This Boardman building is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a data center under the name Carrier Services Group, a name that suggests telecom carrier support work such as interconnection or managed network services. The domain associated with that name resolves but redirects to a parking page, and no business registration or press coverage could be matched to the address. The operator is unconfirmed.

For AI specifically, the absence of published power and cooling capacity means this facility cannot be assessed as a contributor to compute scaling. A carrier-services site is a real category of telecom infrastructure, but it is not the same thing as a large compute campus, and nothing in the record shows it is one.

What the data does not cover: it cannot say whether the building operates as a data center at all, what workload it runs, or how much power it draws. It also cannot say how many of Ohio's other 68 undisclosed facilities are large. The 60.4 MW figure describes only what has been published, not what has been built.
